newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa tax body legislation expected by end-June.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa tax body legislation expected by end-June.

text.p: Legislation providing for the new South African Revenue Services (SARS) should still be tabled in parliament by the end of June, the finance committee heard on Tuesday.

SARS Commissioner Trevor van Heerden told the committee that Cabinet was expected to examine the legislation again on Wednesday and he hoped that he could discuss it with the committee before the end of the month.

He had been asked how SARS was coping with the sudden departure of chief executive Piet Liebenberg last month, apparently after differences of opinion with government on the extent to which SARS would be independent from public sector controls.

The Ministry of Finance had said that it was looking for a replacement for Liebenberg and in the meantime Deputy Minister Gill Marcus was clearing any administrative and technical hurdles faced by SARS.
SARS was established last year after the merger of the Departments of Inland Revenue and Customs and Excise to beef up revenue collection.
